title: Hip and core exercise programme prevents running-related overuse injuries in adult novice recreational runners: a three-arm randomised controlled trial (Run RCT)
authors: Leppänen M, Viiala J, Kaikkonen P, Tokola K, Vasankari T, Nigg B, et al.
population: Adult novice recreational runners (245 female, 80 male) followed for 24 weeks, all doing the same running programme under physiotherapist supervision
findings: Runners were randomised to hip and core exercises (n=108), ankle and foot exercises (n=111), or static stretching control (n=106), performed before running; all groups were physiotherapist-supervised and ran the same programme.
Lower-extremity injury incidence was lower with hip and core than control: HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.45-0.97).
Average weekly prevalence of overuse injuries was 39% lower (PRR 0.61, 95% CI 0.39-0.96) and of substantial overuse injuries 52% lower (PRR 0.48, 95% CI 0.27-0.90) with hip and core exercises.
Ankle and foot exercises did not reduce injuries and had a higher incidence of acute injuries than control (HR 3.60, 95% CI 1.20-10.86).
limitations: Single-country trial with supervised delivery; the abstract does not give exercise dose or frequency. The ankle/foot acute-injury finding rests on few events (wide CI). Control was static stretching, not no intervention.
implications: Include a hip and core strength block in the novice plan, done before runs; set, rep and frequency are not in the abstract, so defaults must come from elsewhere and be labelled grade D.
Do not prescribe an ankle/foot-only routine as injury prevention for novices on this evidence.
Weekly self-reported injury and exposure questionnaires are a usable monitoring input.
